It's faster to do it yourself. That's why you always do.

The ages are a rough guide. The more useful part is how you hand a job over:
1. Do it together.
2. They do it while you watch.
3. They do it and you check.
4. It's theirs.

Start with one job. Give it a few weeks before you judge it.

We're building Bonded, an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android.

#parentingtips #raisingkids

3. Stop when the timer stops, done or not.
4. Then go do something fun together.

Pancakes count.

Try it tonight: ten minutes, everyone at the table, the week out loud.

Ask four questions:
1. Who needs to be where?
2. Who's driving?
3. What needs packing?
4. What's fun this week?

Someone will say 'wait, that's this week?' at least once. That's the point. Then write it where everyone can see it, so the questions don't all come to you.

posts.text:
The same job for everyone sounds fair. It stops being fair when one kid is 12 and the other is 5.

What helps:
1. Give jobs that fit their age.
2. Swap the jobs nobody likes between the kids who can do them.
3. Let them help decide.
4. Change it as they grow.

We're building Bonded, an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android.

Comment WAITLIST and we'll send you the link.

#siblings #parentingtips

metadata.altText: 'That's not fair!' Every day. About who does which job.
And you have to be the judge. Every single time.
Give jobs that fit their age. Matching socks at 5 is a real job. So are dishes at 12.
Swap the jobs nobody likes. The older kids take turns with the trash and the recycling, week by week.
Let them help decide. Ask what feels fair to them first. It's harder to argue with a plan you helped make.
Change it as they grow. What's fair at 6 and 10 isn't fair at 8 and 12.
Join the waitlist. Bonded is an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android. Link in bio.

posts.text:
How do you split jobs between kids who are years apart?

The same jobs for everyone is the simple answer. But the same job is a very different amount of work at 5 and at 12.

What tends to work better: jobs that fit each kid's age, swapping the jobs nobody likes, and asking the kids what feels fair before you decide. A good test: can each kid say why the split is fair?

We're building Bonded, an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android.

posts.text:
Should allowance be linked to chores? Good parents land on both sides, and their reasons are good.

Many families end up in the middle: everyday jobs unpaid, a few bigger jobs paid.

The one version that doesn't work is the one where nobody agreed on anything and payday turns into a fight. Where do you land?

We're building Bonded, an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android.

#allowance #parentingtips

metadata.altText: Should allowance be linked to chores? Good parents land on both sides.
Money talks turn into fights. Most of the time, nobody agreed on the rules.
One side: pay for jobs. Kids learn that work earns money. Saving means more when they earned it.
The other side: some jobs come with living here. Pay for everything, and you may hear 'how much?' every time you ask for help.
Many families do both. Daily jobs don't get paid. Big extra jobs, like washing the car, do.
Whatever you pick, agree before payday. What's paid, how much, and which day. Write it down.

Kids hear about it fast when they forget something. When they do it before anyone asks, it usually gets silence, because nothing went wrong.

Try this:
1. Notice it out loud.
2. Say it the same day.
3. Say what they did, not just 'good job'.

It doesn't need to be a speech. 'You fed the dog before I asked. Thanks.' is plenty.

Fun plans get pushed back when the week is full. The zoo, the bike ride, 'maybe next weekend'.

Try this:
1. On Sunday, plan the week together.
2. Pick one fun thing to look forward to.
3. Share the jobs during the week.
4. On Saturday, go do the fun thing.

Dinners, walks and time together never depend on the jobs. The fun thing is just easier to fit in when nobody is stuck with all of it.

We're building Bonded, an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android.

posts.text:
Weekend plans seem to live or die by Wednesday.

Leave it to Saturday morning and everyone is tired, nobody wants to pick, and it turns into 'maybe next weekend'. Decide midweek, with a rain plan, and it becomes real.

Where are you heading this weekend? Always happy to steal a good idea.

We're building Bonded, an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android.

Comment WAITLIST and we'll send you the link.

metadata.altText: Do your weekend plans fall through? Not because nobody wants to go. Because nobody picked a plan.
And one more Saturday goes by. Everyone is tired, and nobody wants to pick.
Decide on Wednesday. Not on the day. By then it is too late.
Pick three things. What you'll do. When you'll leave. What to do if it rains.
Join the waitlist. Bonded is an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android. Link in bio.

posts.text:
Every family has a list of things they keep meaning to do. The hike. The trip. The place someone talked about two summers ago.

Pick one. Put a date on it. Write it where everyone can see it.

Then tell us yours. This could turn into a very good list.

We're building Bonded, an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android.

Comment WAITLIST and we'll send you the link.

#familytime #familylife

metadata.altText: What has your family been meaning to do for ages? The hike. The trip. The place someone talked about two summers ago.
'Someday' never comes. There's always a busy week in the way.
Pick one thing from the list. Just one. The easiest one.
Put a date on it. Write it down where everyone can see it.
Then tell us yours. Reply with your family's list. We'll share the best ideas, with permission.
Join the waitlist. Bonded is an app that helps your whole family plan the week and share the jobs. It's coming to iPhone and Android. Link in bio.
